title: Generation and Differentiation of Thymic Epithelial Organoids from Adult Mouse Thymus Tissue
author: Willemsen, Yanti, et al.

steps.title: Prepare chemical and growth factor stocks
steps.instruction: Dissolve reagents in the indicated solvents to make the following stock solutions and store at –80 °C for up to 12 months, avoiding repeated freeze‑thaw cycles: N‑acetyl‑L‑cysteine 4 g in 49 mL Milli‑Q water (500 mM); Nicotinamide 12.2 g in 100 mL PBS (1 M); MEGF1 1 mg in 2 mL 0.1 % BSA/PBS (500 µg mL⁻¹); A83‑0150 150 mg in 23.7 mL DMSO (5 mM); FGF7 100 µg in 1 mL 0.1 % BSA/PBS (100 µg mL⁻¹); FGF10 100 µg in 1 mL 0.1 % BSA/PBS (100 µg mL⁻¹); RANK‑ligand 100 µg in 1 mL 0.1 % BSA/PBS (100 µg mL⁻¹); Retinoic acid 10 mg in 3.33 mL DMSO (10 mM); Y‑27632 dihydrochloride 100 mg in 31.2 mL Milli‑Q water (10 mM).

steps.title: Make AdDF+++ basal medium
steps.instruction: Combine Advanced DMEM/F12 (485 mL) with Penicillin‑Streptomycin (10 000 U mL⁻¹) to a final 100 U mL⁻¹ (add 5 mL), HEPE​S 1 M to a final 10 mM (add 5 mL), and GlutaMAX 200 mM to a final 2 mM (add 5 mL) for a total volume of 500 mL. Store at 4 °C for up to 1 month.

steps.title: Formulate expansion medium
steps.instruction: To 477 mL of AdDF+++ add the following supplements to reach 500 mL total: Rspo3‑Fc conditioned medium (100 X) 5 mL (1 X); Noggin‑Fc conditioned medium (100 X) 5 mL (1 X); WNT surrogate‑Fc (0.5 µM final) 500 µL (stock 5 mM); B‑27 supplement without vitamin A (50 X) 50 µL (1 X); EGF 50 µL from 500 µg mL⁻¹ stock (final 50 ng mL⁻¹); FGF7 250 µL from 100 µg mL⁻¹ stock (final 50 ng mL⁻¹); FGF10 250 µL from 100 µg mL⁻¹ stock (final 50 ng mL⁻¹); A83‑01 500 µL from 5 mM stock (final 500 nM); Nicotinamide 1.25 mL from 1 M stock (final 2.5 mM); N‑acetyl‑cysteine 625 µL from 500 mM stock (final 625 µM). Store at 4 °C for up to 1 month. Optionally add Primocin to a final 50 µg mL⁻¹ immediately before use.

steps.title: Add Y‑27632 to expansion medium
steps.instruction: Just before plating dissociated thymic cells, add 50 µL of the 10 mM Y‑27632 stock to 50 mL of the expansion medium to obtain a final concentration of 10 µM. Prepare this mixture immediately before use; for passaging, use the same Y‑27632‑containing medium for the first 2–3 days.

steps.title: Prepare first differentiation medium (DM)
steps.instruction: Mix 98 mL AdDF+++ with 2 mL B‑27 supplement (50 X) to obtain 100 mL total. Store at 4 °C for up to 1 month. (Note: this DM contains the standard B‑27 supplement with vitamin A.)

steps.title: Prepare second differentiation medium (DM+RR)
steps.instruction: Combine 97.79 mL AdDF+++ with 2 mL B‑27 supplement (50 X), 200 µL RANK‑ligand stock (100 µg mL⁻¹) to reach 200 ng mL⁻¹, and 10 µL retinoic acid stock (10 mM) to reach 1 µM. Total volume 100 mL; store at 4 °C for up to 1 month.

steps.title: Thaw and keep BME on ice
steps.instruction: Thaw BME Cultrex Basement Membrane Extract (Growth Factor Reduced, Type 2) at 4 °C for at least 16 h. Keep the thawed BME on ice at all times; it can be stored on ice for up to 1 month and at 4 °C for up to 1 month after thawing.

steps.title: Set up tools and pre‑cool centrifuge
steps.instruction: Gather sterile scissors, forceps, gauze pads, 2 mL microcentrifuge tubes, and a 15 mL conical tube. Pre‑cool the centrifuge to 4 °C and place the BME on ice.

steps.title: Euthanize mice and expose thoracic cavity
steps.instruction: Euthanize five wild‑type C57BL/6 mice (6–12 weeks old) by CO₂ inhalation according to institutional guidelines. Make a midline skin incision from the urethral opening to the lower jaw, extend the incision down the sides toward the knees forming an inverted “Y”, pull back skin and pin to the dissection mat, puncture the diaphragm near the xiphoid process, cut along both sides of the ribcage up to the clavicle, lift and pin ribs to expose the thoracic cavity.

steps.title: Dissect and clean thymic lobes
steps.instruction: Using forceps, lift the ribs and locate the two thin whitish thymic lobes over the heart. Detach surrounding connective tissue and fat with sterile tweezers, then place the thymus on sterile gauze moistened with PBS. Rinse the tissue by repeatedly dipping it in 10 mL of AdDF+++ medium in a 10 cm Petri dish.

steps.title: Transfer thymus to tube with AdDF+++
steps.instruction: Move the rinsed thymus into a 2.0 mL microcentrifuge tube containing 1 mL AdDF+++ medium.

steps.title: Mince thymus into ~0.5 mm² fragments
steps.instruction: Inside the microcentrifuge tube, cut the thymus with sterile scissors into the smallest possible pieces (~0.5 mm²). This fine mincing is critical because the protocol does not use enzymatic digestion.

steps.title: Mechanically dissociate tissue fragments
steps.instruction: Pipette the minced tissue up and down repeatedly with a 1000 µL pipette tip until the suspension becomes homogeneous and can be pipetted smoothly.

steps.title: Pool minced tissue from all thymi
steps.instruction: Repeat the dissection, rinsing, mincing, and mechanical dissociation steps for each of the five thymi, then combine all fragment suspensions into a single 15 mL conical tube.

steps.title: Centrifuge tissue fragments (300 × g)
steps.instruction: Spin the pooled fragments at 300 × g for 3 min at 4 °C. Discard the supernatant and keep the pellet.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet with flamed Pasteur pipette
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL AdDF+++ medium to the pellet and gently resuspend using a glass Pasteur pipette whose tip has been flame‑narrowed in two steps (hold tip in flame a few seconds while rotating). Pre‑wet the pipette by aspirating and expelling 1 % BSA in PBS several times before use.

steps.title: Filter suspension through 100 µm strainer
steps.instruction: Pass the resuspended tissue through a 100 µm cell strainer into a new 15 mL conical tube. Rinse the strainer with an additional 10 mL AdDF+++ medium to recover any remaining fragments.

steps.title: Centrifuge and discard supernatant (500 × g)
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the filtered suspension at 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C. Carefully aspirate all supernatant, leaving the pellet.

steps.title: Repeat resuspension and filtration wash
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 10 mL AdDF+++ medium, repeat the 100 µm strainer rinse (step above), then centrifuge again at 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C and aspirate the supernatant. The resulting cell pellet is ready for downstream organoid culture or analysis.

steps.title: Isolate RNA from organoids
steps.instruction: Collect organoids (as described for replating/passaging). Add ice‑cold PBS up to 12 mL, invert to mix, then centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C. Remove all supernatant, including the translucent BME layer. Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL ice‑cold PBS, add 10 mL more ice‑cold PBS, invert, and centrifuge again at 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C. Discard supernatant and proceed with RNA isolation using any commercial kit.

steps.title: Prepare organoids for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Collect organoids as above, add ice‑cold AdDF+++ medium up to 12 mL, invert, then centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C. Remove all supernatant, taking care to eliminate the BME layer.

steps.title: Enzymatic dissociation with TrypLE
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL TrypLE to the organoid pellet, resuspend thoroughly, and incubate in a 37 °C water bath for 5 min, swirling gently every minute to keep organoids in suspension.

steps.title: Generate single‑cell suspension
steps.instruction: Using a 1000 µL pipette tip with a 20 µL tip attached, vigorously pipette the suspension up and down until the solution becomes cloudy, indicating single‑cell dissociation. Pass the suspension through a 40 µm cell strainer to remove remaining clumps.

steps.title: Wash cells and prepare for staining
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL 1 % FBS‑containing PBS (FACS buffer), mix, and centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C. Discard supernatant, then resuspend the pellet in 1 mL FACS buffer, add another 10 mL FACS buffer, mix, and centrifuge again under the same conditions. Remove all supernatant, leaving a clean cell pellet.

steps.title: Count cells and adjust concentration
steps.instruction: Determine cell number and dilute or concentrate the suspension so that 1 × 10⁶ cells are in 100 µL FACS buffer for each staining condition.

steps.title: Stain cells with fluorophore‑conjugated antibodies
steps.instruction: Resuspend 1 × 10⁶ cells in 100 µL FACS buffer, add the following antibodies at the manufacturers’ recommended concentrations: anti‑mouse Ly‑51‑PE‑Cy7 (cTEC marker), anti‑mouse I‑A/I‑E‑BV421, anti‑mouse CD80‑BV605, and UEA‑1‑Rhodamine (mTEC marker). Incubate on ice for 30 min in the dark.

steps.title: Final wash and resuspend for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL FACS buffer, centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant, and finally resuspend the stained cell pellet in 500 µL FACS buffer. Proceed to flow cytometry analysis.

description: Thymic epithelial cells (TECs) play a crucial role in T cell development and immune system homeostasis by providing essential signals for thymocyte maturation and selection.2,3 The ability to generate thymic epithelial cell organoids from adult mouse thymus tissue offers a powerful in vitro system to study thymic epithelial biology, immune cell interactions, and potential regenerative approaches for thymus dysfunction. Unlike traditional 2D culture systems, three-dimensional TEC organoids provide a long-term expandable model with the potential to support studies on thymic development, aging, and related disorders. To generate thymic epithelial cell (TEC) organoids from adult mouse thymus tissue, proper preparation and handling of tissue samples are critical. This protocol requires the use of adult C57BL6 mouse thymus tissue (6–12 weeks old) and emphasizes immediate processing after isolation to ensure cell viability. Prepare all reagents, including defined growth factor-enriched medium and extracellular matrix (ECM), before starting the protocol. Use aseptic techniques throughout the process to prevent contamination during tissue dissociation, 3D embedding, and organoid culture. Additionally, ensure access to equipment and materials for downstream analyses, such as flow cytometry, qPCR, and immunostaining, which are used to assess organoid differentiation and functionality. Researchers should obtain appropriate institutional ethical approvals before conducting experiments involving animal tissue. Adherence to institutional guidelines for animal care and handling is essential to ensure compliance with ethical research standards.
